project.objective: Did Sebastiano Mingazzini and his wife Lucia Silvestrini of Castel Bolognese, Ravenna, Italy have a son named Simone, born 1860, in addition to their three known children (b. 1849-1853)?

questions.question: Did Sebastiano Mingazzini and his wife Lucia Silvestrini have a son named Simone born circa 1860 in Castel Bolognese, Ravenna, Italy?
questions.rationale: The research objective asks whether a fourth child named Simone (born c. 1860) existed beyond the three known children (born 1849–1853). This question is directly and fully testable against Italian civil registration birth records (stato civile, beginning 1866 in post-unification Emilia-Romagna) and pre-unification Catholic parish baptismal registers (battesimi) for Castel Bolognese. A birth circa 1860 sits right at the boundary of both record regimes, making a two-pronged search necessary. The question is formulated as a single, bounded fact-question with named individuals and a specific place and approximate date, satisfying GPS question-formulation criteria.

items.rationale: Italian civil registration (stato civile) began in Castel Bolognese in 1866 (loc_001). FamilySearch collection 1947700 (Italy, Ravenna, Ravenna, Civil Registration, Tribunale, 1866-1943) holds Nati (birth) volumes for 1866, 1867, 1868, 1869, and 1870 at 100% record-searchable. Searching for all births naming Sebastiano Mingazzini as father in Castel Bolognese will: (a) establish the family corpus after 1866 — confirming the couple is in the record set; (b) identify any child named Simone born 1866-1870 (the question asks about c.1860 but the actual birth year may be off); (c) provide crucial negative evidence if no Simone appears; and (d) surface other children who, when they later married, might have filed supporting documents (allegati) referencing a pre-1866 sibling Simone. This is the indexed, free primary search and must come first.

FamilySearch collection 1708706 (Italy Births and Baptisms, 1806-1900) is an indexed collection of Italian birth and baptismal records spanning both the civil registration and church record eras. It may include parish baptismal extracts for Castel Bolognese circa 1860 that were microfilmed and indexed separately from the civil registration volumes. Because a birth c.1860 falls in the Papal States ecclesiastical gap (loc_001) where only parish registers exist, this collection is the best indexed source for that period. Search for 'Simone Mingazzini' with father 'Sebastiano' and mother 'Lucia Silvestrini' in Castel Bolognese, and also a surname-only search for all Mingazzini in Castel Bolognese 1855-1865 to catch variant spellings or siblings.

Per the record-type guide, for unindexed parish registers the full-text co-occurrence search is the highest-yield approach when indexed search stalls. The pre-1866 parish baptismal registers (battesimi) for Castel Bolognese are not name-indexed on FamilySearch (loc_001 confirmed no parish volumes in volume_search for this period). A full-text search on the co-occurrence of 'Mingazzini' and 'Silvestrini' as two separate required terms across the FamilySearch full-text corpus may surface a baptismal entry, a marriage supporting document referencing both parents, or another record that mentions the couple together. Route to search-full-text skill. Do not scope to a specific collection ID — run unscoped across the whole corpus.

Italy instituted universal male conscription under the Legge della leva militare (1865) after unification. Men born in 1860 would be called for military enrollment (leva) circa 1880-1882. The ruoli matricolari (military conscription rolls) list each conscript by name, birth date, birthplace, and typically the names of both parents — making them direct evidence that a man named Simone Mingazzini existed and was born to Sebastiano Mingazzini. These records are held at the Archivio di Stato di Ravenna (provincial level) and may be partially available on FamilySearch, Antenati, or other Italian digital archives. Search FamilySearch for Italian military records covering Ravenna province, circa 1878-1884 enrollment year. If a Simone Mingazzini born c.1860 in Castel Bolognese is present, his parentage line in the roll will confirm or deny Sebastiano as his father.

Allegati matrimoni (marriage supporting documents) for 1866 — image group 004876621_007 — are full-text searchable on FamilySearch (loc_001). When residents of Castel Bolognese married after 1866, the supporting documents filed with the civil registrar typically included an estratto di battesimo (baptismal extract) documenting the bride or groom's birth, even if that birth predated civil registration. If any of Sebastiano and Lucia's older children (born 1849-1853) or a son Simone (born c.1860) married in Castel Bolognese in the late 1860s-1870s, their marriage allegati would contain a baptismal extract referencing the pre-1866 birth. Use full-text search on 'Mingazzini' in this volume. Also search allegati nati 1866-1867 (image groups M93F-TB2 and M93F-TBV) which contain supporting documents for birth registrations — parents sometimes attached church certificates documenting prior-born children when registering a new birth.

Antenati (antenati.cultura.gov.it), the Italian National Archives portal, independently digitized civil registration records from 1866 for Castel Bolognese. It may have image coverage not duplicated in FamilySearch's collection 1947700, or name indexes built from different transcription sources. Fallback for plan item 1 if FamilySearch's indexed search returns no Mingazzini births or if birth volumes are missing pages. Use 'Search by location' for Castel Bolognese. This is a free, authoritative external repository.

MyHeritage hosts 'Italy Births and Baptisms, 1806-1900' (collection 30210) with independent indexing of Italian church and civil records. This collection may have baptismal entries from Castel Bolognese parish registers that were transcribed differently or separately from FamilySearch collection 1708706 (plan item 2). A search for Simone Mingazzini (or all Mingazzini) in Castel Bolognese 1855-1865 may surface a record not found on FamilySearch. Accessible at a FamilySearch center for free. Fallback for plan item 2.

proof_summaries.exhaustive_search_summary: Three search strategies were executed: (1) FamilySearch collection 1947700 (Italy, Ravenna, Ravenna, Civil Registration, Tribunale, 1866-1943), the indexed civil registration corpus for Ravenna province — yielded the marriage bann for Simone Mingazzini, dated 24 March 1887, Solarolo, directly naming his parents (pli_001, log_003, positive). (2) FamilySearch collection 1708706 (Italy Births and Baptisms 1806-1900) for a baptismal record of Simone Mingazzini born 1854-1864 in Castel Bolognese — zero results (pli_002, log_004, negative), confirming the loc_001 finding that pre-1866 parish registers for Castel Bolognese are not name-indexed online. (3) Full-text co-occurrence search '+Mingazzini +Silvestrini' across the entire FamilySearch corpus — 120 results, first 20 examined; no Simone baptismal record found, but contextual corroboration found in marriage records for siblings Francesca (1870, Castel Bolognese) and Giovanni (1875 and 1886, Castel Bolognese and Solarolo) naming the same parents (pli_003, log_005, partial). Unsearched sources that could corroborate or advance to proved: (a) pre-1866 parish baptismal registers for Castel Bolognese, held at the Archivio Diocesano di Imola (not consulted); (b) military conscription rolls (ruoli matricolari) for Ravenna province, Archivio di Stato di Ravenna, which would record Simone born 1859 circa 1879-1881 and list his parents (not consulted). Research exhaustiveness not formally declared because these repositories remain unsearched.
proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Simone Mingazzini, Son of Sebastiano Mingazzini and Lucia Silvestrini

**Research question:** Did Sebastiano Mingazzini and his wife Lucia Silvestrini have a son named Simone, born circa 1860 in Castel Bolognese, Ravenna, Italy?

**Conclusion:** The preponderance of available evidence strongly suggests that Simone Mingazzini, born approximately 1859 in Castel Bolognese, was a son of Sebastiano Mingazzini (tree person GQSW-B3V) and Lucia Silvestrini (tree person GQS4-95W).

---

### Primary Evidence

The central document is an indexed transcription of a civil marriage bann (*pubblicazione di matrimonio*) dated 24 March 1887, published in Solarolo, Ravenna: "Italia, Ravenna, Ravenna, Stato Civile (Tribunale), 1866-1943," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XWTT-TBL8 : accessed 2026-08-03), entry for Simone Mingazzini and Angela Bassi, marriage bann, 24 March 1887, Solarolo, Ravenna.

This source is a **derivative** record — a FamilySearch name-index transcription of the original civil register. The original image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSDJ-D3G6-L) was not examined; all facts below derive from the indexed transcription only.

The bann identifies the groom as **Simone Mingazzini**, born approximately 1859 in Castel Bolognese, occupation *Colono*, son of **Sebastiano** [Mingazzini — surname not indexed, implied from groom's surname] and **Lucia Silvestrini**.

Under the Italian *Codice Civile* of 1865, parties to a civil marriage proceeding were legally required to declare their parentage under oath to the registrar (*ufficiale dello stato civile*), and the allegati (supporting documents) typically included a baptismal extract. The groom's declaration of parentage was therefore both legally sworn and subject to registrar verification — though the underlying allegato was not examined.

**Identity analysis — five matching identifiers:**

1. **Given name:** "Simone" — matches the child named in the research question.
2. **Surname:** "Mingazzini" — matches the father's family name.
3. **Birth year:** approximately 1859 — consistent with "circa 1860" in the research question (the index records birth year, likely derived from a baptismal extract).
4. **Birthplace:** Castel Bolognese, Ravenna — exact match with the expected birthplace.
5. **Mother's surname:** "Silvestrini" — an uncommon and distinctive surname, exactly matching the known wife of Sebastiano Mingazzini (GQS4-95W in the tree).

The father's given name "Sebastiano" matches GQSW-B3V. No alternative candidate is known — no other Sebastiano Mingazzini with a wife named Lucia Silvestrini is documented in the Castel Bolognese area.

**Source classification:** The birth-year and birthplace assertions are classified as **secondary information** — the groom cannot have firsthand cognitive knowledge of his own birth — reported by himself as informant, with likely derivation from a baptismal extract submitted with the allegati. The parentage assertion ("son of Sebastiano and Lucia Silvestrini") is classified as **primary information** — the groom himself is the informant, stating facts within his personal knowledge under legal oath. The evidence type for all parentage and identity facts is **direct** — the record explicitly names the persons and relationships sought.

**Limitation:** The father's surname was not indexed in the bann. "Mingazzini" is implied from the groom's own surname and from the research context, but is not confirmed from the indexed transcription. Examination of the original image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSDJ-D3G6-L) would confirm whether the father's full surname appears in the original document.

---

### Corroborating Context

A full-text co-occurrence search for "+Mingazzini +Silvestrini" across the FamilySearch corpus (log_005) identified three records that contextualize the family:

- **1870 Marriage Proclamation, Castel Bolognese** (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSQT-53X6-W): names "Francesca Mingazzini," "Sebastiano," and "Lucia Silvestrini" — likely the marriage bann for Francesca Mingazzini (GQSW-TJW), listing her parents as Sebastiano and Lucia Silvestrini.
- **1875 Marriage Proclamation, Castel Bolognese** (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSQT-53D6-S): names "Giovanni Mingazzini" and "Lucia Silvestrini."
- **1886 Marriage Supplement, Solarolo** (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSXB-RSSZ): names "Giovanni Mingazzini," "Lucia Silvestrini," and "Sebastia[no]" — a sibling's civil marriage record from the same municipality where Simone published his 1887 bann, one year earlier.

These records were not extracted (they fall outside q_001's scope), but they corroborate that Sebastiano Mingazzini and Lucia Silvestrini are documented as parents of multiple children in Ravenna civil records, and that the family had genuine connections to Solarolo.

---

### Negative Findings

A search of FamilySearch collection 1708706 (Italy Births and Baptisms 1806-1900) for Simone Mingazzini born 1854–1864 in Castel Bolognese returned zero results (log_004). This confirms the locality-guide finding (loc_001) that pre-1866 parish baptismal registers for Castel Bolognese — which would be the primary record type for a birth circa 1859, in the Papal States ecclesiastical gap before Italian civil registration reached this area — are not name-indexed in the FamilySearch corpus. The absence is a research gap, not evidence of non-existence.

---

### Research Scope and Limitations

The following sources remain unsearched:

- **Pre-1866 parish baptismal registers** (*Libri dei battesimi*) for the parish of Castel Bolognese, held at the Archivio Diocesano di Imola. These would be the original record of Simone's birth and would directly confirm his parents.
- **Military conscription rolls** (*ruoli matricolari*) for Ravenna province, held at the Archivio di Stato di Ravenna. Men born in 1859 were enrolled circa 1879–1881; these rolls list each conscript's birth date, birthplace, and parents' names, and would independently corroborate the parentage.

Because these repositories remain unsearched, research exhaustiveness has not been formally declared.

---

### Tier Assessment

The conclusion is assessed at **probable** rather than proved for four reasons: (1) only one formal source was found; (2) that source is a derivative record, not the original civil register; (3) the pre-1866 baptismal register was not consulted; and (4) research exhaustiveness has not been formally declared. The five matching identifiers — including the distinctive surname "Silvestrini" — and the absence of any conflicting evidence support a strong probable finding. Consultation of the original image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSDJ-D3G6-L), the parish baptismal registers at the Archivio Diocesano di Imola, or the military conscription rolls at the Archivio di Stato di Ravenna would advance this conclusion toward proved.

localities.guide_markdown:
## Castel Bolognese, Ravenna, Emilia-Romagna, Italy — Locality Guide (1850–1870)

### Jurisdictional Context
Castel Bolognese was part of the **Papal States** until 1860, when it joined the Kingdom of Sardinia; it became part of the unified **Kingdom of Italy** in 1861. This transition is the single most important fact for record availability in this period: **civil (stato civile) registration did not exist** in Castel Bolognese between 1816 and 1865. A birth in 1860 was recorded only in the Catholic parish baptismal register (*battesimi*).

### Record Regimes, 1850–1870

#### Pre-1866 (1850–1865): Ecclesiastical Records Only
- **Primary source**: Catholic parish baptismal register (*battesimi*) kept by the local parish church in Castel Bolognese, under the Diocese of Imola.
- **FamilySearch availability**: NONE found. No parish register volumes for Castel Bolognese appeared in volume_search for this period. The FamilySearch wiki page section for 'Church Records' for Castel Bolognese is empty.
- **Where to look**: Diocesan Archive of Imola (*Archivio Diocesano di Imola*) or the local parish directly. Antenati does NOT cover this period.
- **Napoleonic gap note**: Napoleonic civil registration (1806–1815) is available as browse-only images at FamilySearch Catalog (catalog 3026019, held at Archivio di Stato di Bologna, sez. Imola) — but this does not extend to 1860.

#### Post-1866: Civil Registration — Well Digitized
- **Italy, Ravenna, Ravenna, Civil Registration (Tribunale), 1866–1943** (FS collection 1947700) — **indexed & images**.
  - Nati (births): 1866–1870 volumes all at **100% record-searchable** (name-indexed). Searchable via `record_search`.
  - Matrimoni (marriages): 1866–1870 at 100% indexed.
  - Morti (deaths): 1866–1870 at 60–86% indexed.
- **Registri dello stato civile di Castel Bolognese (Ravenna) 1866–1929** (catalog 1315917) — images only.
- **Italia, Ravenna, Castel Bolognese. Stato civile, Tribunale: 1869–1945** (catalog 2519721) — images.
- **Antenati** (antenati.cultura.gov.it): civil registration images and indexes from 1866; search by location for Castel Bolognese.

#### Allegati (Supporting Documents)
Marriage and birth supporting document bundles (*allegati*) for 1866–1867 are digitized but largely browse-only (some full-text searchable). The 1866 *allegati matrimoni* (M93F-TBK) is **full-text searchable**. These bundles may contain baptismal extracts (*estratti di battesimo*) for children born before 1866 when they later married.

#### Decennial Indexes (Indici Decennali)
Browse-only name indexes for births, deaths, and marriages 1866–1875 exist (image groups 007847845_054, _064, _059) but are not name-indexed or full-text searchable.

### External Resources
- **Antenati** (antenati.cultura.gov.it) — Italian National Archives civil registration portal, 1866+
- **Italy Births and Baptisms 1806–1900** (FS collection 1708706 / MyHeritage) — may include church-extracted baptism records
- **italianparishrecords.org** — external index of Italian parish records
- **FamilySearch Research Guide for Italy** (BYU PDF) — covers ecclesiastical record strategy

### Key Research Strategy Note
For a birth **circa 1860** in Castel Bolognese: the direct record (baptismal register) is not currently online. The practical research path is: (1) search the 1866–1870 indexed civil births for any Mingazzini births listing Sebastiano and Lucia as parents — this establishes the family corpus and may bracket the gap; (2) search marriage allegati for older Mingazzini children marrying after 1866, whose supporting documents may include a baptismal extract for a c. 1860 birth; (3) for a definitive answer on a pre-1866 birth, the Diocesan Archive of Imola must be consulted directly.
